practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word profile of a fictional student. Include an interest, a specific experience, its significance, and a realistic learning goal.

practice.sample_answer_en: Amy enjoys explaining how everyday objects work. Last term, she helped a younger student repair a bicycle light. She discovered that a simple drawing made her instructions easier to follow. That experience encouraged her to join the design club. She now wants to improve her drawing skills and test her explanations with classmates. Her goal is to create a short repair guide that a beginner can actually use.
practice.reading_en: Sam is a new member of the school media club. He enjoys photography, but his interest is not only in attractive pictures. Last spring, he photographed the school garden while volunteers were replacing broken signs. A younger student later told him that the pictures explained the work more clearly than a list of tasks. Sam began to notice how images could help people understand a process. This term, he wants to create a photo guide for new garden volunteers. He plans to ask a beginner to follow the guide before sharing it with the club. For Sam, a successful picture is one that helps someone act.

practice.sample_answer_en: Our class started a reading corner last month. We moved two shelves into an empty classroom and invited students to suggest books. Since then, we have collected enough stories for the first shelf. Several younger students have visited the corner, but we have not opened it every day yet. We still need to agree on a schedule. The first visits gave us useful questions to discuss at our next meeting.
practice.reading_en: Last term, Amy joined a team that was designing a quieter lunch area. The team interviewed students in May and presented its first plan in June. Since then, the school has provided a small room, and volunteers have moved some tables into it. Amy has written a short welcome notice, but the team has not agreed on opening hours yet. The room is ready for a trial, not for a permanent opening. Amy says the earlier interviews helped the team choose the location. She believes the next step is to watch how students use the room during a short trial and then review the schedule.

His fingers are sore today because he has been practicing a new song. He can now play its opening smoothly, but he has not learned the whole piece yet. He plans to record another practice session and listen for places that need attention.
practice.reading_en: For the past two weeks, Amy has been preparing a short talk for the science club. She has been practicing in an empty classroom since Monday because the library is busy. Today her voice sounds tired, and several pages of notes are spread across a desk. She has been rehearsing the opening, but she has not decided how to explain the final experiment. Her partner suggests another picture instead of another paragraph. Amy stops practicing to draw it. Although she is no longer speaking at this moment, the tired voice and notes still show evidence of her recent work. The talk itself is not finished.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word description of a fictional school team. Use a defining relative clause with a subject relative word and one with an object relative word. Explain why a particular person or resource is suitable.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞介紹虛構校園團隊，使用一個關係詞作主詞的限定子句和一個作受詞的限定子句，並解釋特定人物或資源為何合適。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our team needs a student who can explain simple repairs patiently. Amy is a good choice because she helped new volunteers last term. The guide that she wrote uses pictures instead of long paragraphs. We also need someone who can test the instructions without extra help. Sam can do that because he has not used the equipment before. His questions will show us which parts of the guide need clearer explanations.
practice.reading_en: The garden club needs volunteers for two different jobs. Students who enjoy working outdoors can help repair signs. Students who prefer writing can improve the volunteer guide. Amy offers to work on the guide that Sam wrote last term. She thinks the photographs are useful, but some instructions are difficult to follow. The student who tests the revised guide should be new to the garden. An experienced volunteer might understand an unclear instruction simply because they already know the task. The club therefore asks Pip, a new member, to try the guide. His questions help the writers identify information that a beginner needs.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the club want a beginner to test the guide?

practice.sample_answer_en: Amy, who leads our media club, is preparing an exhibition. Our main camera, which the school bought last year, is ready to use. Students who have finished their captions can help arrange the photographs. Others still need to check names and dates. Sam, who enjoys organizing displays, has offered to plan the entrance. practice.reading_en: Amy leads a small media club with three members: Sam, Pip, and herself. Amy, who joined the club last year, now organizes its exhibition. She writes two possible notices. The first says, "Students who have finished their captions can arrange the display." This notice invites only the students with completed captions. The second says, "The students, who have finished their captions, can arrange the display." In that notice, all the students being discussed have finished. Amy chooses the first because Pip is still checking a date. The main camera, which Sam borrowed from the office, is ready. Their preparations are progressing, but the members are not all at the same stage.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word paragraph about improving a fictional school service. Use a that clause as an object and a what or how clause as a subject. Explain one observation and one question still needing an answer.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞說明如何改善虛構校園服務，使用 that 子句作受詞及 what 或 how 子句作主詞，交代一項觀察和一個待解問題。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our team noticed that several students arrived at the wrong room for tutoring. What they need is a notice with a clear room number. The current notice gives the day and time but leaves out the location. We do not know why the number was removed, so we should ask the organizer before changing the file. How students find the notice also matters, because an accurate message is useful only if they can see it.
practice.reading_en: The student council is reviewing its tutoring notice. Amy explains that several new students went to the library instead of Room Five. What confused them was a missing room number, not the starting time. Sam checks the original message and confirms that it gives Tuesday at four but no location. The team wants to know why the room number disappeared from the final version. They cannot answer that question from the notice alone. How students receive the message also matters: some see a printed copy, while others read it on a phone. The council decides to check both versions before announcing a correction, so that the same mistake does not remain in one format.

questions.prompt_en: What information was missing from the notice?
questions.answer_en: The room number was missing.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the council check both the printed and phone versions?
questions.answer_en: Students receive the notice in both formats, so correcting only one could leave the mistake in the other.

questions.prompt_en: Can the council conclude who removed the room number? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. The notice shows the missing information but does not explain why it disappeared or who removed it.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word email to a fictional school organizer. Explain your context, ask two specific embedded questions, and close politely without assuming approval.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞寫信給虛構校園活動負責人，交代背景、提出兩個具體嵌入式問句，並客氣結尾，不預設已獲許可。
practice.sample_answer_en: Dear Ms. Lee, Our media club is preparing photographs for the school exhibition next Friday. Could you tell me whether the spare camera is available on Thursday afternoon? I would also like to know where we should return it after use. We need it for indoor pictures and can collect it after our last class. Thank you for considering our request. We will wait for your reply before changing our plan. Best regards, Amy
practice.reading_en: Amy wants to borrow a camera for the school exhibition. Her first message says only, "Can we have the camera?" The organizer cannot tell which camera she means or when the club needs it. Amy revises the message. She explains that the club is taking indoor photographs on Thursday afternoon. She then asks, "Could you tell me whether the spare camera is available then?" A second question asks where the camera should be returned. The new message is polite, but its usefulness also comes from the specific details. Amy has not received permission yet, so she keeps another plan available and waits for the organizer's reply.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word profile of a fictional student applying for a club role. Connect an earlier difficulty, a specific response, and a current goal. Include a claim supported by the experience.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞介紹申請社團職務的虛構學生，連結較早遇到的困難、具體回應與目前目標，並提出有該經驗支持的看法。
practice.sample_answer_en: Amy hopes to help train new members of the design club. Last term, a student could not follow the instructions she had written. Instead of blaming the reader, Amy watched the student try each step and added clearer labels. She has since been testing her guides with beginners before sharing them. This experience suggests that she is willing to revise her work in response to feedback. She now wants to make the club handbook easier to use.
practice.reading_en: Sam is applying to help organize the school exhibition. His profile begins with a mistake: last year, he placed several captions beside the wrong photographs. A visitor pointed out the problem, and Sam checked every label before the next group arrived. Since then, he has been using a numbered plan when arranging displays. He also asks another student to compare the plan with the finished arrangement. In his application, Sam says this experience taught him to check information rather than trust his memory. He now wants to help new club members prepare their first display. The profile supports a claim about careful improvement, but it does not show that Sam can manage every part of a large event alone.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word connected profile of a fictional student. Link a past experience, ongoing learning, and a future goal. Include one relative clause and one noun clause, and keep claims supported by details.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞寫虛構學生的連貫介紹，連結過去經驗、持續學習及未來目標，包含一個關係子句與一個名詞子句，並以細節支持看法。
practice.sample_answer_en: Amy, who enjoys explaining practical skills, wants to help new science club members. Last term, she discovered that her instructions were unclear when a beginner followed the wrong step. She has been testing her guides with new readers since then. The comments she collects help her identify missing information. What she values most is seeing someone complete a task independently. By the next club meeting, she will have revised the guide for one simple experiment.
practice.reading_en: Pip is preparing a profile for the school design club. His first draft lists several interests but does not explain how they connect. He revises it around one experience. Last term, a new student struggled to follow a map that Pip had drawn. Pip asked where the student had become confused and changed the labels. Since then, he has been testing his maps with people who do not know the building. What he wants to learn next is how to make directions clearer without adding too much text. By the club interview, he expects to have completed a revised map. His profile now connects a problem, a response, continuing practice, and a realistic goal.
